cos101-university-mock-0001.explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) executes program instructions.

cos101-university-mock-0003.explanation: A keyboard sends data into the computer; the others are output devices.

cos101-university-mock-0004.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) structures web pages.

cos101-university-mock-0006.explanation: RAM is volatile storage; ROM is non-volatile.

cos101-university-mock-0007.explanation: Excel is application software (a spreadsheet), not an operating system.

cos101-university-mock-0008.explanation: A program is a sequence of instructions executed by a computer.

cos101-university-mock-0009.explanation: A GUI presents windows, icons and menus instead of text commands.

cos101-university-mock-0010.explanation: Machine language (binary) is executed natively; other languages are translated first.

cos101-university-mock-0011.explanation: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a web address.

cos101-university-mock-0012.explanation: Excel is a spreadsheet application for tabular data and calculation.

cos101-university-mock-0013.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits; IPv4 addresses are 32 bits.

cos101-university-mock-0014.explanation: Oracle DBMS stores and manages structured data; the others are a browser, a language and an OS.

cos101-university-mock-0015.explanation: The CPU performs the processing — the 'brain' analogy.
